note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, values, conditions and quotes; both capture the T.O. steel and solar envelope elevations and the member section designations. The only substantive difference is that A repeats the L3x3x1/4" fact one extra time (three claims vs. two), so A carries slightly more duplication. Both sets make the same misbinding of C3X6 as a 'Beam' (it is a channel designation) and both use vague entities ('component', 'framing member', 'member') with heavy duplication of W6X20, W10X12, HSS4X4X1/4, HSS4X6X1/4 and C8X11.5. Neither set captures the elevation datums (FIRST FLR 2'-4", GRADE LEVEL 0"), overall dimensions (32'-0", 27'-8", 8'-8 5/8") or the 1/4"=1'-0" scale.
remarks: Both sets bind C3X6 to 'Beam' although the C prefix denotes a channel; both also repeat the same section designations under generic and typed entities (e.g. 'component | specification | W10X12' alongside 'framing member | section | W10X12'). The four elevation blocks in the text layer are hard to map unambiguously to the four named elevations (A1 East, A3 South, C1 West, C3 North), so condition assignments such as C8X11.5 to 'East' and L3x3x1/4" to 'East' cannot be verified from the text layer alone and may be swapped; both sets make these assignments identically. Important facts both sets miss: FIRST FLR 2'-4", GRADE LEVEL 0", overall widths 32'-0" and 27'-8", 8'-8 5/8" and 8'-8 1/2" dimensions, and the 1/4" = 1'-0" scale.
